hypothesis: Across the human growth period (ages 2-19), the log-log slope of mean body weight against mean standing height is close to 3, and a cubed height curve reproduces most of the age-shape of the weight curve.
pass_criterion: Using NHANES examined children and adolescents aged 2-19, compute sex-specific mean weight (BMXWT) and mean standing height (BMXHT) for each single year of age (RIDAGEYR), using MEC exam weights. Regress ln(mean weight) on ln(mean height) across ages. The claim passes if the pooled slope is between 2.7 and 3.3 with a 95% CI that includes 3 or lies wholly within 2.7-3.3, and R² is at least 0.95. In addition, the curve W_hat = k*H^3, with k fitted once, must explain at least 80% of the variance of mean weight across ages (R² of observed on predicted weight).
fail_criterion: The claim fails if the pooled log-log slope is below 2.5 or above 3.5, or if its 95% CI excludes the 2.5-3.5 interval. It also fails if the k*H^3 curve explains less than 60% of the across-age variance of mean weight. Results between these thresholds are inconclusive.
interpretation: Thompson's 'linear dimension' is measured as standing height (stature). 'Volume, and therefore weight' is body mass, assuming roughly constant density. 'Tend to vary as the cubes' is read as a log-log allometric exponent near 3 for growth over age. 'Mainly though not wholly' is operationalised as the cubic model explaining at least 80% of the weight-curve shape, with some residual allowed. Modern reinterpretation: the test uses population-mean cross-sectional growth curves by age, not longitudinal individual growth. It uses NHANES survey data from recent decades rather than 19th-century measurements. Within-age individual scaling is not tested, because the claim concerns change during growth.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES publishes public-use Body Measures files with measured weight (BMXWT, kg) and standing height (BMXHT, cm) for children and adults. The Demographics files give age in years (RIDAGEYR), sex (RIAGENDR) and exam sample weights (WTMEC2YR). Together these cover ages 2-19 across many survey cycles, enough to build the age-specific mean curves for weight and stature that the test needs.
